paragraphs: Dawn in the barracks yard. Forty recruits in their line, with shields too heavy and spears too long, and Straton walking in front of them: one eye, a limp from a war nobody remembers, and a voice that carries to the harbour.
You have been a soldier of Massalia for a season. You can stand in a line. Straton does not yet think you can do anything else.

choices.text: Take your place in the line.

paragraphs: Today it is the shield wall, hour after hour, until the line moves like one man or Straton loses his voice.

choices.text: Hold the wall with the line.
choices.result: By the third hour you have stopped feeling your shoulder, which Straton says is the whole point.
You go down twice and get up twice, and the third time it is his shield that gives a hand's width. "Again tomorrow," he says, which from Straton is a garland.

otherwise.result: He puts you in the dust three times, and the third time you stay there. "Better here than on a field."

paragraphs: Before noon a boy is at the gate asking for you by name. He is the grandson of old Euboula, who keeps the bakery under the potters' quarter and has been a friend of your family since before you were born.
Three men have come to her ovens every morning for a week, asking a drachma a day "to keep the fire safe". Yesterday she said no, and they broke her jars. They are there now.

choices.text: Go at once, as you are.
choices.result: You go at a run in your drill bronze, the boy trotting ahead.

choices.text: Bring Dion and Lysis from the line.
choices.result: They come for the price of a jug of wine tonight, and bring their shields without being asked.

paragraphs: Three men among the broken jars: sellswords paid off from the tyrant of Syracuse's wars, their pay long drunk, with nothing left but their bronze and the habit of being feared.
The biggest, Bryas, has a Corinthian helmet pushed back on his head and one of Euboula's loaves in his fist. "A recruit. She sent for a recruit."

choices.result: He learned to fight in taverns, and you learned from Straton. On the third pass he is on the flagstones with your spear-butt at his throat. His friends run and leave their shields and helmets where they dropped them.

otherwise.result: He knocks you down twice and you get up both times; the third time he stays down. You win, and the whole street saw how close it was.

choices.text: Shield up, and drive them out.
choices.result: You do what the line does: shield up, head down, one step at a time. Three men with no line are only three men. Their bronze stays in the yard.
Ten drachmae buys their backs. They go out laughing in all their bronze, and Bryas takes the loaf.

choices.text: Lock shields and drive them out.
choices.result: Three against three, but only one side is a line. They drop their shields to run faster.
Ten drachmae buys their backs. They go out laughing in all their bronze, and Dion laughs at you all the way back.

paragraphs: Three shields with the paint knocked off, two helmets, a sword in a cracked scabbard and a bundle of spears. Old bronze, but good. Euboula looks at her broken jars, and then at the pile.

choices.text: Sell it to the armourer by the arsenal.
choices.result: He bites the sword and pays sixty drachmae without asking where it came from. Bronze is bronze.

choices.text: Hand it in at the city arsenal.
choices.result: The clerk writes it down with your name beside it, and the magistrates pay the bounty on bronze taken from men who broke the peace: ten drachmae, and a clerk who tells everyone.

choices.text: Let Euboula sell it for her jars.
choices.result: "Half for the jars and half for you, or I bake it into the bread."

paragraphs: By evening everyone in the barracks has heard. Straton finds you at the water trough.

choices.result: He tells it again to the whole barracks at supper, better than you did.
"Good. Then you won't mind doing it again." He moves you to the front rank tomorrow.

So does he. He does not need to.
